ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Mahatma Gandhi — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for lightheadedness on standing and a near-fall in hot weather

text.paragraph: Lightheaded on standing and nearly fell this morning. [S]

Mr. Gandhi is a 70-year-old man with stage 2 hypertension on amlodipine 5 mg, underweight by long choice, who came in the same day after nearly falling. During the past three days of very hot weather he kept his usual 5 km morning walk and his community work but drank less than usual, about 1 L a day. This morning, standing up from his spinning, the room went grey and he caught hold of the doorframe; he did not fall, hit his head, or lose consciousness. He has felt lightheaded on standing since yesterday. His home blood pressure this morning was 104/62 sitting. He has had no chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, or black stools, and no new medicines. He is not fasting and has eaten normally. He took amlodipine this morning. [S]

list.item:
Dehydration with orthostatic hypotension (E86.0). Volume depletion from heat and low fluid intake, made worse by amlodipine. BUN 28 mg/dL and creatinine 1.02 mg/dL (eGFR 79), up from 0.82 in February; sodium 141 and potassium 4.0 mmol/L are normal. ECG not needed: no chest pain, palpitations, or syncope, and the rhythm is regular. [S]
Oral fluids now and about 2.5 L a day while the heat lasts, with a pinch of salt and some citrus juice as he likes.
Hold amlodipine for two days, then restart if home systolic pressure is above 120 sitting and he is not dizzy on standing.
Walk in the cooler early morning and rest at midday.
Sit before standing and stand slowly; call the same day for fainting, chest pain, or a fall.

Hypertension (I10). Pressure low today from volume depletion. [S]
Home readings sitting and standing twice a day; telephone check in three days.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and osteoporosis monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Telephone check in three days with home readings. Blood pressure and nutrition review in July as planned. Next scheduled visit 1940-07-13: blood pressure, nutrition, vitamin B12 and D, and bone health review at about five months. [S]
